# Imajin — You compose. Imajin orchestrates. Signed. Legible.

Generated 2026-10-26 UTC from merged working tree based on source 6e4b1d28aa1b5e7888a5a827f407aa54e82974ce, release comparison v0.8.27..6e4b1d28a.
This is a source inventory, not deployment evidence or a permission grant.

Imajin is Agentic Relation Management. The kernel serves six primitives:
Attestation · Communication · Attribution · Settlement · Discovery · Revocation.
Identity is their subject, not a seventh primitive. Proof of history records who
asserted what; a signature does not establish the truth of the assertion.
User signatures, node-witnessed records and unsigned logs have different strength.

Kernel: apps/kernel, canonical origin https://jin.imajin.ai, dev localhost:3000.
Internal services: broker-agent and corpus; corpus production is assigned to gx10
in the recorded deployment posture, not the kernel host. Apps built on Imajin
(events, coffee, dykil, learn, links, market) have independently owned repositories.
Use their scoped-token contract and published @ima-jin/* SDKs, not kernel imports.
Workspace imports use @imajin/*. private:true is not evidence of publication;
the generated package table in README.md links checked public registry metadata.
License: Imajin Network License (INL) v1.0, source-available, not MIT.

## Integration and safety
- App-hosted upstreams: PUT /connections/api/upstreams declares {upstreams:[{id,
  origin,credentialHeader,credentialPrefix,paths:[{path,methods}]}]} on the caller's
  existing registry app. App-service token + connectors:upstream:read + live operator
  approval required. GET with appDid/upstreamId lets a personal member review it.
  POST /connections/api/upstreams/connection takes {appDid,upstreamId,origin,secret,
  orgContextDid?} in the member's own human session; origin must match the declaration.
  This connect step is API-only: connect/status responses include sorted plain-text
  permissions such as ["GET /me"]. When disconnected, this is the current review list,
  not proof that the member approved it.
  GET status uses appDid/upstreamId query; DELETE takes those selectors in JSON,
  retaining revoked rows and vault tombstones even after app/declaration withdrawal.
  Existing OAuth consent grants connectors:upstream:read, optionally :write, per app.
  POST /connections/api/upstreams/call takes {memberDid,upstreamId,path,method,body?,
  reason?} as the app service, never a caller-selected app DID. GET/HEAD use read;
  every other method needs explicit :write in token, live operator ceiling AND
  member's app grant, plus reason member-request|app-workflow|scheduled-task.
  Exact declared paths/methods only, HTTPS public egress pinned at connect, no redirects.
  Kernel-only key injection; {status,body} response, no upstream headers/stream/errors,
  2 MiB response and 16 KiB request limits. Credential echoes are refused.
  Destination/header/prefix and canonical path/method pairs are member-bound.
  Adding, changing or removing a path/method requires reconnecting; reordering does not.
  Earlier destination-only bindings also require one reconnect. Successful calls are
  recorded against member/app/org with signed reason/outcome metadata, never request body.
  Authorized upstream failures are recorded too; refusals write nothing permanent.
  Admission limits run before any database read.
  Shared authorizeMemberConnection gates both this path and personal Postman MCP;
  org-admin suspension is enforced only inside that gate, before vault access.
  See /connections/api/spec for the full contract and custody/deadline semantics.
- Personal Postman MCP: GET/POST/DELETE /connections/api/external-mcp/postman
  requires the member's own human session, never org act-as or app lifecycle access.
  POST seals a write-only secret plus optional orgContextDid; DELETE revokes custody
  and writes a signed vault tombstone, retaining history. Tier 0 only; no generic fetch/export.
  POST /connections/api/external-mcp/postman/rpc accepts tools/list or tools/call.
  Apps need connectors:mcp:read, live member consent and active registration;
  app-service calls also need operator scope approval and memberDid. Tagged org
  standing is checked each call. The kernel injects credentials only to the fixed
  official Postman target; only reviewed saved-data reads are allowed, no writes
  or runCollection/live requests. See /connections/api/spec.
  Admission is per process: 20/member/minute, 60/app/minute and 4 calls in flight;
  429/503 admission refusals write nothing permanent. No transaction spans Postman I/O.
  Signed audit follows the exchange; reconnect tombstones the prior sealed field.
- Org connection administration: GET/POST /auth/api/org-connections,
  UI /auth/members while acting as the org. Human session + live owner/admin +
  auth-service access required; non-admin/app/agent requests refuse. POST takes
  {action:suspend|resume,reason,connectionId} or {action,reason,provider}, never both
  selectors. Reason is nonblank, at most 500 characters; never enter credentials.
  Provider suspension covers future connections too. Individual/service policies
  resume separately. Removal persists per-connection suspensions with remover
  actor/reason; re-add and reconnect do not resume. Policies are org-scoped;
  personal use is untouched. Signed history is retained, keys never handed out.
  Both proxy paths return the same generic 403 before custody access. Already
  admitted calls may finish. GET returns metadata and latest 100 audit events only.
  See /auth/api/spec; no credentials, fields or bindings in admin responses.
- MCP cycle_status and cycle_run require cycle:run plus the live connector grant.
  Both return the caller's registry horizon {depth,targetDepth:12,deficit,zones:
  {tail,middle,near,head,past},noStepsPublished}; belowDepth:{deficit} is present
  only below target. cycle_run captures this before starting phases.
  No published steps returns depth 0 and "No horizon steps published yet", not
  an error; a drained horizon is distinct. No cycle yet returns correlationId:null
  and state:not_started. Explicit foreign/non-cycle ids remain not_found.
  Contracts: /jin/api/spec x-mcp-tools and MCP tools/list. No harness reads or refill.
- App sign-in begins on the app's createLoginHandler route. Keypair consent
  POST /api/auth/authorize issues a 60-second single-use code bound to app,
  authenticated subject, live authorization, callback and state. The app signs
  its exchange at POST /auth/api/apps/token and uses only the returned subjectDid
  and attestationId for its session. See /auth/api/spec and auth-client README.
- Internal GET /api/cron/app-authorization-code-cleanup requires the vault cron
  bearer, not a session or app token. Every ten minutes it deletes only
  auth.app_authorization_codes past one hour from consumption (or expiry when
  unconsumed), returning {ok:true,deleted}. Live codes and grace-boundary rows stay.
- Warp briefs: GET/PUT /jin/api/brief-settings (human session, warp-scoped
  owner/admin act-as only), UI /jin/brief-settings. Default full-text stores
  exact outgoing UTF-8 in a private immutable signed media asset. The final
  prompt/message, including corpus context, is capped at 1048576 UTF-8 bytes
  (1 MiB); oversized HTTP requests return 413 and MCP tools name the limit.
  Each dispatch/resume/follow-up loop event carries brief
  {hash,assetId,storage,browserTesting}; settings changes are node-signed.
  A provider rejection/network failure retains the recorded brief plus a signed
  warp.brief.dispatch_failed containing only hash, assetId, upstreamStatus and
  errorClass. Hash-only stores no text; anyone holding a guess of a brief's text
  can confirm it against the plain SHA-256 hash. Earlier assets remain.
  /jin Runs opens and verifies the brief's SHA-256.

- /jin Decisions reads /jin/api/operator-approvals?view=acting&source=decision&history=true.
  Open decision:card rows are oldest first; ruled pending apply and applied history
  are collapsed. Subject and recorded signerDid filters are display-only. Missing
  agent provenance is explicit, never inferred from a harness. Rulings reuse the
  existing operator-approvals/{proposalId}/decision countersignature contract.
- Five standing tiers: soft, preliminary, established, steward, operator.
  Soft identities have no actor signing key; route authorization still applies.
- Key-based registration derives did:imajin:<base58(public-key bytes)>.
  DFOS linking is separate and optional. Do not substitute a SHA-256 DID derivation.
- Session JWTs use EdDSA. Host-only cookies are the default; domain scope is an
  explicit rollback. /auth/api/session/soft resolves an identity without setting
  a cookie. Use the auth spec for verified login/onboarding contracts.
- Registered apps use user-delegated or session-less app-service tokens with
  explicit scopes. Owner/admin membership alone never substitutes for a required
  delegation grant. Never fall back to the personal DID after act-as refusal.
- Vault supports v1 node-sealed and v2 delegation-grant entries. Tier 0 remains
  node-controlled, not zero-custody; optional Tier 1 is not universal deployment.
  Secrets are sealed through kernel tools, never pasted into code, logs or docs.
- Bank-details:v1 uses GET/PUT/DELETE /auth/api/bank-details with human-session,
  auth-scoped owner/admin authorization. Financial fields are individually sealed;
  public metadata carries references and visibility only. Saves replace immutable
  records; revocation retains history. Tier 1 saves fail closed. No settings UI,
  invoice disclosure or generic secret-fetch access is implied.
- Legal-entity:v1 uses /auth/legal-entity and /auth/api/legal-entity; each legal
  name/address field has independent public/on-consent/never release. Consumers use
  getLegalEntity, not generic media access or metadata copies.
- /cloudflare/api/grants lists the authenticated grantee's live exact-zone
  metadata, never credentials; an acting identity cannot widen that list.
- SSH CA lifecycle and signing are purpose-scoped. /api/vault/ssh-ca/sign uses
  live operation grants, signed principal/forced-command/host restrictions, TTL
  bounded by grant expiry and a 900-second maximum. Revoking authority stops new
  signing, not already-issued certificates. Hosts must enforce public trust and
  principals; allowedHosts is issuance policy, not an OpenSSH host restriction.
- .github/actions/vault-ssh-deploy verifies GitHub OIDC for an exact repository
  and environment plus immutable repository/owner IDs in signed grant scope.
  Legacy GitHub grants without IDs require operator re-grant. Optional allowedRefs
  pins exact full workflow_ref strings. Each jti can mint once until token expiry;
  only signature/origin-verified policy refusals are audited. Unverified OIDC and
  key-fetch failures return generic 401 with no audit signing or writes.
  GitHub refusals are deduplicated for all time by issuer-separated jtiHash;
  expired/not-yet-valid/stale or missing/malformed-jti tokens write nothing.
  id-token:write and a protected environment
  are required, on a dedicated self-hosted no-swap runner with startup orphan cleanup.
  The per-job private key stays in non-swappable tmpfs; pinned known-hosts is
  mandatory. See docs/deploy/vault-ssh-deploy.md, not a stored deploy-key recipe.
- Corpus GitHub partitions belong to the registry-resolved source-owner group DID;
  workspace sources remain principal-owned. Live owner-issued corpus grants are
  checked before claims or credential lookup. Membership/stub creation grants no
  access. OAuth connector refs belong to that owner; no personal-connector,
  GITHUB_TOKEN, GH_TOKEN or gh CLI credential fallback. Follow apps/corpus/README.md
  for explicit connector selection and the signed, row-preserving owner migration.
- Inference passthrough uses /infer/v1/*, principal-based token minting and the
  usable model catalog. The release updater requires successful exact-SHA
  production deployment and mint-backed health before promotion/rollback.
  See deploy/infer-passthrough/README.md; source is not live-host rollout evidence.
- MJN is receipt-backed/withdrawable in the receipt's currency; activity emissions
  are non-withdrawable MJNx. No fixed CHF peg, automatic conversion or token date
  is asserted. Remaining model questions are annotated in the whitepaper/RFC-12.
- .fair builder defaults include protocol/platform/node/buyer components; do not
  infer universal 2% fees or mandatory manifest verification on every settlement
  path. Consult current settlement implementation and the whitepaper's caveats.
- Chat uses the kernel HTTP server's WebSocket, not a separate ws process.
  TLS in transit; plaintext at rest on the hosting node in chat.messages_v2.content.
  Push notifications carry the first 200 characters of the message preview.
  End-to-end encryption (MLS with mandatory hybrid post-quantum encryption) is
  planned under #1070, not implemented; no forward-secrecy or post-compromise guarantee.

## How to read the inventory

Every tracked App Router route handler is listed below, including internal,
development-only, discovery and non-API handlers. Presence is not public access:
read its implementation and service spec for auth, schemas, errors and rollout.
Templates use {id}; {path...} denotes catch-all (optional catch-all is documented
by its source). OPTIONS is explicit when exported; framework implicit HEAD/OPTIONS
are not separately enumerated. Page components are not API route handlers.
Corpus is Express, not App Router: its separate /spec operation definitions follow.
Specs are contracts, not deployment inventories. Unmapped spec-only operations
are omitted from the implemented reference and reported in the #2028 run-log.

## v0.8.28 contract delta (merged source, not deployment)

- POST /jin/api/app-secrets accepts sync, generate, set, rotate and revoke.
  Sync proposes only new validated manifest name/kind slots; a human operator
  countersigns apps:secrets-sync. It does not generate/grant values or change
  DID, keys, slug, claims, removals, existing kinds or non-secret permissions.
  A new generated slot needs separate signed apps:secrets-generate; any prior
  grant history (including revoked tombstones) refuses Generate. Operator-supplied
  slots use masked Set and a separate approval. No value is revealed.
  See docs/app-self-secrets-operator.md; #3124.
- POST /pay/api/payment-requests/{id}/checkout admits issuer, recipient or a
  human controlling the recipient organization under current owner/admin plus
  pay-service access. Member/maintainer, agent, removed membership and excluded
  pay access do not gain control. payerPersonDid stays distinct from callerDid
  and paidByDid; paidByDid determines settlement payer attribution.
  HTTP 403 code not_party_to_request differs from payer_not_controlled.
  EMT by-handle retains its opaque-handle capability and payer-control gate,
  not the card party gate; its 403 payer error now carries the code. See #3126.
- tag-release.yml close-out creates missing GitHub Releases with generated notes
  and rolls open issues/PRs into the lowest open next patch milestone in the same
  major/minor series before closing the released milestone. No next milestone
  means warning/no close; existing Releases and closed milestones are skipped.
  Failure is visible and independent of npm publishing. Production review is
  unchanged. See docs/npm-publishing.md; #3120.

## Provider-billed reconciliation

Provider-billed reconciliation setup (#3136): use /auth/connectors/anthropic or
/auth/connectors/openai, Billing (admin) key. GET/POST/DELETE
/{anthropic|openai}/api/billing-key are authenticated kernel-root routes.
GET returns only presence/pending booleans; POST seals or rotates {token};
DELETE revokes billing custody, not inference scopes, and retains signed history.
Never send credentials through chat. Explicitly grant the provider's :billing
scope after sealing. /jin Spend shows billed: not connected when keys are absent;
the next usage-billed-ingest cron populates source=api rows for reconciliation.

# Service contracts from /spec definitions

## Contract: /api/spec

Source: apps/kernel/app/api/spec/route.ts. Version: 1.0.0.
Declared server bases: https://imajin.ai, https://dev-www.imajin.ai.
Legacy service-relative paths are mapped to actual kernel handler paths below;
parameter placeholders use the handler's spelling. These are not extra aliases.
Every mapped operation follows with parameter names, body media types, security
and response codes. Unmapped spec-only operations are excluded (see #2028 run-log).
Fetch the served spec/source for full schemas and validation; absence of a
declaration never overrides the implementation's authorization.

- GET /api/health — System health check; security: not declared (not proof of anonymous access); responses: 200
- POST /api/subscribe — Email subscription; security: not declared (not proof of anonymous access); responses: 200

## Contract: /auth/api/spec

Source: apps/kernel/api-spec/auth.yaml. Version: 2.0.0.
Declared server bases: https://{node}.imajin.ai/{service}, http://localhost:3000/{service}.
Legacy service-relative paths are mapped to actual kernel handler paths below;
parameter placeholders use the handler's spelling. These are not extra aliases.
Every mapped operation follows with parameter names, body media types, security
and response codes. Unmapped spec-only operations are excluded (see #2028 run-log).
Fetch the served spec/source for full schemas and validation; absence of a
declaration never overrides the implementation's authorization.

- GET /auth/api/bank-details — Read own non-secret bank-details projection and rail capabilities; security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 401, 403, 404, 503
- PUT /auth/api/bank-details — Seal and replace own bank-details record; body: application/json (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 201, 400, 401, 403, 503
- DELETE /auth/api/bank-details — Revoke own document and supersede every active vault grant for its fields; security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 401, 403, 404, 503
- GET /auth/api/identities/{did}/domains — List domain bindings for an identity owner or active admin; parameters: path:did (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]},{"bearerAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 401, 403, 500
- POST /auth/api/identities/{did}/domains — Add a pending DNS ownership binding; parameters: path:did (required); body: application/json (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]},{"bearerAuth":[]}]; responses: 201, 400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 500
- POST /auth/api/identities/{did}/domains/{domain}/verify — Check public TXT proof and persist signed domain verification; parameters: path:did (required), path:domain (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]},{"bearerAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 500, 503
- DELETE /auth/api/identities/{did}/domains/{domain} — Revoke and remove a domain binding; parameters: path:did (required), path:domain (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]},{"bearerAuth":[]}]; responses: 204, 400, 401, 403, 404, 500
- GET /auth/api/identities/{did}/domains/public — Public verified domains and signed ownership evidence for profiles; parameters: path:did (required), query:domain; security: []; responses: 200, 400, 500
- GET /.well-known/imajin.json — Discover the current host's verified ownership; security: []; responses: 200, 400, 404
- GET /api/domain-check — On-demand TLS/routing authorization check; parameters: query:domain (required); security: []; responses: 200, 400, 404
- GET /auth/api/groups/{groupDid}/transfer-owner — Current owner and pending ownership invitation; parameters: path:groupDid (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]},{"bearerAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 401, 403, 404
- POST /auth/api/groups/{groupDid}/transfer-owner — Owner invites another person to take ownership; parameters: path:groupDid (required); body: application/json (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]},{"bearerAuth":[]}]; responses: 201, 400, 401, 403, 404, 409
- DELETE /auth/api/groups/{groupDid}/transfer-owner — Owner cancels the matching pending transfer; parameters: path:groupDid (required); body: application/json (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]},{"bearerAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 400, 401, 403, 404, 409
- POST /auth/api/groups/{groupDid}/transfer-owner/accept — Named person accepts ownership and any required membership invitation; parameters: path:groupDid (required); body: application/json (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]},{"bearerAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 500
- GET /.well-known/agent/{id} — Read a person's public reach card; parameters: path:id (required); security: []; responses: 200, 404, 500
- POST /auth/api/agents/{did}/reach — Ask the boolean reach gate or deliver a message; parameters: path:did (required); body: application/json (required); security: [{"reachBearer":[]},{}]; responses: 200, 400, 401, 403, 404, 429
- POST /auth/api/agents/{did}/reach/{reachId}/status — Read your own reach receipt and principal-signed reply; parameters: path:did (required), path:reachId (required); body: application/json; security: [{"reachBearer":[]},{}]; responses: 200, 400, 401, 404
- GET /api/health — Service health check; security: not declared (not proof of anonymous access); responses: 200
- GET /auth/.well-known/kernel-signing-key — Fetch the kernel's Ed25519 signing public key(s) (#2244); security: []; responses: 200, 503
- POST /auth/api/challenge — Create a signing challenge (API token flow); body: application/json (required); security: not declared (not proof of anonymous access); responses: 200, 400, 404
- POST /auth/api/authenticate — Submit signed challenge and receive an API token; body: application/json (required); security: not declared (not proof of anonymous access); responses: 200, 400, 401
- POST /auth/api/login/challenge — Create a login challenge by handle or DID (session cookie flow); body: application/json (required); security: not declared (not proof of anonymous access); responses: 200, 400, 404, 429
- POST /auth/api/login/verify — Verify signed challenge and set session cookie; body: application/json (required); security: not declared (not proof of anonymous access); responses: 200, 400, 401
- POST /auth/api/logout — Clear session cookie; security: not declared (not proof of anonymous access); responses: 200
- GET /auth/api/session — Get current session from cookie; security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 401
- POST /auth/api/session/soft — Create or retrieve a soft DID session from email; body: application/json (required); security: not declared (not proof of anonymous access); responses: 200, 400, 429
- POST /auth/api/register — Register a new keypair-backed DID identity; body: application/json (required); security: [{},{"appServiceAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 201, 400, 401, 403, 409, 429
- POST /auth/api/onboard — Initiate email-based onboarding or login — sends verification email; body: application/json (required); security: not declared (not proof of anonymous access); responses: 200, 400, 403, 429, 502
- POST /auth/api/onboard/send — Ask the node to privately email an app-owned order's buyer an onboarding link; body: application/json (required); security: [{"appServiceAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 400, 401, 403, 404, 429, 502, 503
- GET /auth/api/onboard/verify — Complete email verification — mints soft DID and sets session cookie; parameters: query:token (required); security: not declared (not proof of anonymous access); responses: 302, 400
- GET /auth/api/onboard/poll — Poll for verification status of an onboard token (cross-tab handoff); parameters: query:handle (required); security: not declared (not proof of anonymous access); responses: 200, 400, 429, 500
- POST /auth/api/onboard/claim — Claim a session via one-shot handoff token (cross-tab handoff); body: application/json (required); security: not declared (not proof of anonymous access); responses: 200, 400, 404, 410, 429, 500
- GET /auth/api/search — Search public identities by handle, display name, or DID; parameters: query:q, query:limit; security: []; responses: 200, 500
- GET /auth/api/lookup/{id} — Look up identity by DID; parameters: path:id (required); security: not declared (not proof of anonymous access); responses: 200, 404
- POST /auth/api/validate — Validate an API token and return identity; body: application/json (required); security: not declared (not proof of anonymous access); responses: 200
- GET /auth/api/apps — List apps this identity has added or authorized; parameters: query:for, query:placement; security: [{"cookieAuth":[]},{"bearerAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 400, 401, 403
- GET /auth/api/apps/directory — Browse every active app registered on this node with a nav placement; security: [{"cookieAuth":[]},{"bearerAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 401, 403
- PUT /auth/api/apps/{slug} — Add a registered app to your navigation in one click; parameters: path:slug (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]},{"bearerAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 401, 403, 404
- DELETE /auth/api/apps/{slug} — Remove explicit membership without revoking app authorization; parameters: path:slug (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]},{"bearerAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 401, 403, 404
- POST /auth/api/apps/token — Mint a short-lived, scoped app token for a third-party app holding a user's app.authorized attestation (#1069,; body: application/json (required); security: not declared (not proof of anonymous access); responses: 200, 400, 401, 403, 404
- POST /auth/api/apps/token/service — Mint an app-tier (keyholder) service token — no user delegation (#1141); body: application/json (required); security: not declared (not proof of anonymous access); responses: 200, 400, 401, 403, 404
- POST /auth/api/apps/token/verify — Stateless verification of an app token minted by /api/apps/token or /api/apps/token/service (#1069); body: application/json (required); security: not declared (not proof of anonymous access); responses: 200, 400, 401, 403
- POST /auth/api/verify — Stateless verification of a signed message; body: application/json (required); security: not declared (not proof of anonymous access); responses: 200
- GET /auth/api/access/{did} — Check whether the authenticated requester has access to a resource DID; parameters: path:did (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 401
- GET /auth/api/identity/{did} — Resolve a DID to its public key and metadata; parameters: path:did (required); security: [{},{"cookieAuth":[]},{"bearerAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 404
- GET /auth/api/identity/{did}/agents — A principal's serving agents and their live connection state (#2407, RFC-31 Phase 1); parameters: path:did (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]},{"bearerAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 401, 403, 500
- GET /auth/api/identity/{did}/chain — Get the DFOS identity chain for a DID; parameters: path:did (required); security: not declared (not proof of anonymous access); responses: 200, 404
- GET /auth/api/identity/{did}/keys — Get current key state for the authenticated identity; parameters: path:did (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 401
- POST /auth/api/identity/{did}/rotate — Rotate keys by submitting an updated DFOS chain log; parameters: path:did (required); body: application/json (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 401, 404, 429
- POST /auth/api/identity/{did}/sign — Node witnesses a payload on behalf of an authorized identity; parameters: path:did (required); body: application/json (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]},{"bearerAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 401
- GET /auth/api/identity/{did}/verify — Verify DFOS chain and check DB consistency for a DID; parameters: path:did (required); security: not declared (not proof of anonymous access); responses: 200, 404
- POST /auth/api/identity/present-chain — External onboarding — present a DFOS chain log to create or retrieve a did:imajin alias; body: application/json (required); security: not declared (not proof of anonymous access); responses: 200, 400, 422, 429
- POST /auth/api/identity/verify-chain — Internal — verify a DFOS chain log and resolve identity; body: application/json (required); security: not declared (not proof of anonymous access); responses: 200, 400
- GET /auth/api/resolve/dfos/{dfosDid} — Resolve a did:dfos to its linked did:imajin identity; parameters: path:dfosDid (required); security: not declared (not proof of anonymous access); responses: 200, 404
- POST /auth/api/documents — Create and first-sign a document request as the effective identity; body: application/json (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 201, 400, 401, 403
- GET /auth/api/documents — List documents where the effective identity is author or signer; parameters: query:role; security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 401, 403
- GET /auth/api/documents/{id} — Read a document and signer identities as an authorized party; parameters: path:id (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 401, 403, 404
- GET /auth/api/documents/{id}/content — Preview or download only the hash-bound document; parameters: path:id (required), query:download; security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 401, 403, 404, 409
- POST /auth/api/documents/{id}/decline — Decline as the effective account's pending party; parameters: path:id (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 401, 403, 404, 409, 410
- POST /auth/api/documents/{id}/amend — Propose an independently signed amendment as the effective identity; parameters: path:id (required); body: application/json (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 201, 400, 401, 403, 404, 500
- POST /auth/api/documents/{id}/sign — Sign as the effective account's pending party; parameters: path:id (required); body: application/json (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 400, 401, 403, 409
- POST /auth/api/documents/{id}/verify — Compare a saved file against the signed hash and verify recorded signatures; parameters: path:id (required); body: multipart/form-data (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 400, 401, 403, 404, 413
- GET /auth/api/attestations/types — Discover registered attestation types; security: not declared (not proof of anonymous access); responses: 200
- POST /auth/api/attestations — Issue a new attestation; body: application/json (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]},{"bearerAuth":[]}]; responses: 201, 400, 401, 403, 409

- POST /auth/api/attestations/countersign — Countersign a pending attestation (witness/subject signs to make it bilateral); body: application/json (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]},{"bearerAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 401, 403, 404, 409, 422

- POST /auth/api/keys/retrieve — Retrieve an encrypted key from secure storage; body: application/json (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 404

- POST /auth/api/mfa/email/setup — Initiate email MFA setup — sends verification code; body: application/json (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 200
- POST /auth/api/mfa/email/verify-setup — Complete email MFA setup by verifying the code; body: application/json (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 400
- POST /auth/api/mfa/email/send — Send an email MFA code (during login); body: application/json (required); security: not declared (not proof of anonymous access); responses: 200
- POST /auth/api/mfa/email/disable — Disable email MFA for the current identity; security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 200
- POST /auth/api/mfa/totp/setup — Initiate TOTP setup — returns QR code / secret; security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 200
- POST /auth/api/mfa/totp/verify — Verify TOTP code and enable TOTP MFA; body: application/json (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 400
- POST /auth/api/mfa/totp/challenge — Validate a TOTP code during login challenge flow; body: application/json (required); security: not declared (not proof of anonymous access); responses: 200, 401
- POST /auth/api/mfa/totp/disable — Disable TOTP MFA for the current identity; security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 200
- POST /auth/api/onboard/generate — Generate onboarding materials (keys, DID document) before registration; body: application/json (required); security: not declared (not proof of anonymous access); responses: 200
- GET /api/spec — Serve the OpenAPI spec YAML; security: not declared (not proof of anonymous access); responses: 200

- GET /auth/api/grants — List the authenticated delegator's own grants; parameters: query:grantId; security: [{"cookieAuth":[]},{"bearerAuth":[]}]; responses: 200
- DELETE /auth/api/grants/{grantId} — Revoke an entire grant; parameters: path:grantId (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]},{"bearerAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 403, 404

- DELETE /auth/api/grants/{grantId}/capabilities/{capability} — Revoke exactly one capability, without touching its siblings (#1882 item 4); parameters: path:grantId (required), path:capability (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]},{"bearerAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 403, 404
- POST /auth/api/grants/{grantId}/renew — Extend a grant's lease (grants are leases with expiry); parameters: path:grantId (required); body: application/json; security: [{"cookieAuth":[]},{"bearerAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 400, 403, 404, 409
- POST /auth/api/internal/verify-delegation — Internal — may agentDid act for principalDid? (#1887 dual-read acting-for check); body: application/json (required); security: [{"internalKeyAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 400, 401, 500
- POST /auth/api/internal/grants/introspect — Resolve delegated authority at execution time (internal, fail-closed); body: application/json (required); security: [{"internalKeyAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 401, 500
- POST /auth/api/knock — External agent knocks, declaring the principal it wants to serve (#1883); body: application/json (required); security: not declared (not proof of anonymous access); responses: 200, 201, 400, 401, 403, 404, 429
- GET /auth/api/knock/pending — List the authenticated principal's own pending, unexpired knocks; security: [{"cookieAuth":[]},{"bearerAuth":[]}]; responses: 200
- POST /auth/api/knock/{knockId}/accept — Mint-on-accept — zero grants (#1883); parameters: path:knockId (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]},{"bearerAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 403, 404, 409
- POST /auth/api/knock/{knockId}/decline — Discard a pending knock — no identity was ever created; parameters: path:knockId (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]},{"bearerAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 403, 404, 409
- POST /auth/api/attestations/turn-evidence — Signed batch ingest of agent.turn.evidence — tool I/O as the committed boundary of a turn (#1978); body: application/json (required); security: []; responses: 200, 201, 400, 403, 422, 429
- GET /auth/api/verify/turn/{hash} — Public, no-auth verification of a turn claim against its signed tool-call evidence (#1978); parameters: path:hash (required); security: []; responses: 200, 400, 404, 429

## Contract: /chat/api/spec

Source: apps/kernel/api-spec/chat.yaml. Version: 2.0.0.
Declared server bases: https://{node}.imajin.ai/{service}, http://localhost:3000/{service}.
Legacy service-relative paths are mapped to actual kernel handler paths below;
parameter placeholders use the handler's spelling. These are not extra aliases.
Every mapped operation follows with parameter names, body media types, security
and response codes. Unmapped spec-only operations are excluded (see #2028 run-log).
Fetch the served spec/source for full schemas and validation; absence of a
declaration never overrides the implementation's authorization.

- GET /api/health — Service health check; security: not declared (not proof of anonymous access); responses: 200
- GET /chat/api/session — Get current chat session — verifies JWT and returns enriched identity with profile; security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 401
- GET /chat/api/capabilities — Get current user's capabilities based on identity tier; security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 401
- GET /chat/api/access/{did} — Proxy access check to auth service — forwards session cookie server-to-server; parameters: path:did (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 401
- GET /chat/api/conversations — List v2 conversations for authenticated user — includes unread counts and DM participant enrichment; security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 401
- POST /chat/api/conversations — Create a new v2 conversation — direct type requires trust graph membership; body: application/json (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 201, 400
- GET /chat/api/conversations/unread — Get unread message counts — returns total and per-conversation breakdown; security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 200
- GET /chat/api/conversations/{id} — Get v2 conversation by URL-encoded DID — verifies access via auth service; parameters: path:id (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 404
- PATCH /chat/api/conversations/{id} — Update conversation name — only the creator can update; auto-creates if not exists; parameters: path:id (required); body: application/json (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 403
- DELETE /chat/api/conversations/{id} — Delete conversation (creator only) — cascades to messages, reactions, and read records; parameters: path:id (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 403, 404
- GET /chat/api/conversations/{id}/messages — Get paginated messages for a conversation — includes inline reactions; parameters: path:id (required), query:limit, query:before; security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 404
- POST /chat/api/conversations/{id}/messages — Send a message — soft DIDs blocked; content must be an object; auto-creates conversation if missing; parameters: path:id (required); body: application/json (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 201, 403
- PUT /chat/api/conversations/{id}/messages/{msgId} — Edit a message (author only) — content must be an object; parameters: path:id (required), path:msgId (required); body: application/json (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 403, 404
- DELETE /chat/api/conversations/{id}/messages/{msgId} — Soft delete a message — author can always delete; others need conversation access; parameters: path:id (required), path:msgId (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 403, 404
- GET /chat/api/conversations/{id}/participants — List conversation participants — proxies to auth service members endpoint; parameters: path:id (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 404
- POST /chat/api/conversations/{id}/participants — Add a participant — delegates to auth service; parameters: path:id (required); body: application/json (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 201
- POST /chat/api/conversations/{id}/read — Mark a v2 conversation as read — upserts last-read timestamp; parameters: path:id (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 200
- POST /chat/api/conversations/{id}/upload — Upload media to a conversation (25 MB max) — images are auto-resized and thumbnailed; parameters: path:id (required); body: multipart/form-data (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 400
- PUT /chat/api/d/{did} — Create or rename an app-owned identity conversation; parameters: path:did (required); body: application/json (required); security: [{"bearerAuth":[],"cookieAuth":[]},{"bearerAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 400, 401, 403, 500
- GET /chat/api/d/{did}/messages — Get paginated messages for a DID-keyed conversation — includes inline reactions; parameters: path:did (required), query:limit, query:before; security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 403
- POST /chat/api/d/{did}/messages — Send a message to a DID-keyed conversation — soft DIDs blocked; auto-creates conversation; node signs payload; parameters: path:did (required); body: application/json (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 201, 403
- PATCH /chat/api/d/{did}/messages/{msgId} — Edit a DID-keyed message (author only); parameters: path:did (required), path:msgId (required); body: application/json (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 403, 404
- DELETE /chat/api/d/{did}/messages/{msgId} — Soft delete a DID-keyed message (author only); parameters: path:did (required), path:msgId (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 204, 403, 404
- POST /chat/api/d/{did}/messages/{msgId}/reactions — Add a reaction to a DID-keyed message; parameters: path:did (required), path:msgId (required); body: application/json (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 201, 400, 404
- DELETE /chat/api/d/{did}/messages/{msgId}/reactions — Remove a reaction from a DID-keyed message; parameters: path:did (required), path:msgId (required); body: application/json (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 204
- PATCH /chat/api/d/{did}/context — Merge context into a DID-keyed conversation; parameters: path:did (required); body: application/json (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]},{"bearerAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 400, 401, 403
- GET /chat/api/d/{did}/members — Get members of a DID-keyed conversation via pod membership — resolves names from auth service; parameters: path:did (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 401, 403
- POST /chat/api/d/{did}/read — Mark a DID-keyed conversation as read; parameters: path:did (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 401, 403
- GET /chat/api/messages/{msgId}/reactions — List grouped reactions on a v2 message — returns per-emoji counts with current user's react status; parameters: path:msgId (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 404
- POST /chat/api/messages/{msgId}/reactions — Add a reaction to a v2 message — idempotent; returns updated reaction counts; parameters: path:msgId (required); body: application/json (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 200
- DELETE /chat/api/messages/{msgId}/reactions — Remove a reaction from a v2 message — returns updated reaction counts; parameters: path:msgId (required); body: application/json (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 200
- GET /chat/api/invites — List active (non-revoked) invites for a conversation; parameters: query:conversationId (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 403
- POST /chat/api/invites — Create an invite link for a conversation; body: application/json (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 201
- GET /chat/api/invites/{id} — Get invite info (public — for preview before joining); parameters: path:id (required); security: not declared (not proof of anonymous access); responses: 200, 404, 410
- POST /chat/api/invites/{id} — Accept a conversation invite — increments use count and returns conversation DID; parameters: path:id (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 403, 410
- DELETE /chat/api/invites/{id} — Revoke a conversation invite (creator or conversation member); parameters: path:id (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 403, 404
- GET /chat/api/keys — Get own public key bundle with unused pre-key count; security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 404
- POST /chat/api/keys — Upload or update public key bundle — signature is verified server-side; body: application/json (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 400
- GET /chat/api/keys/{did} — Get public keys for a DID (public endpoint) — consumes one one-time pre-key if available; parameters: path:did (required); security: not declared (not proof of anonymous access); responses: 200, 404
- GET /chat/api/lookup/{did} — Resolve DID to handle and name (proxies to auth service); parameters: path:did (required); security: not declared (not proof of anonymous access); responses: 200
- GET /chat/api/profile — Proxy profile lookup by handle to profile service; parameters: query:handle (required); security: not declared (not proof of anonymous access); responses: 200, 404
- GET /chat/api/ws-token — Get a short-lived token for WebSocket authentication — exchanges session cookie for token; security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 401
- POST /chat/api/ws-token/validate — Validate a WS auth token (internal — used by ws-server); body: application/json (required); security: not declared (not proof of anonymous access); responses: 200, 401
- GET /chat/api/conversations-v2 — List conversations (v2 — returns ConversationV2 objects with DID-based identifiers); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 401
- POST /chat/api/d/{did}/members/leave — Leave a DID-based conversation; parameters: path:did (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 401, 404
- DELETE /chat/api/d/{did}/members/{memberDid} — Remove a member from a DID-based conversation; parameters: path:did (required), path:memberDid (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 200
- GET /chat/api/participants/{did}/conversations — List conversations a participant (by DID) is part of; parameters: path:did (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 200
- POST /chat/api/participants/migrate — Migrate participant records (e.g. guest-to-hard DID upgrade); body: application/json (required); security: [{"bearerAuth":[]}]; responses: 200
- GET /chat/start — Find or create a DM conversation then redirect to it — used by chat open deep-link; parameters: query:did (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 302, 307

## Contract: /jin/api/spec

Source: apps/kernel/api-spec/jin.yaml. Version: 2.1.0.
Declared server bases: https://{node}.imajin.ai/{service}, http://localhost:3000/{service}.
Legacy service-relative paths are mapped to actual kernel handler paths below;
parameter placeholders use the handler's spelling. These are not extra aliases.
Every mapped operation follows with parameter names, body media types, security
and response codes. Unmapped spec-only operations are excluded (see #2028 run-log).
Fetch the served spec/source for full schemas and validation; absence of a
declaration never overrides the implementation's authorization.


Warp brief contract: Node-witnessed brief descriptor on each kernel Warp dispatch/resume loop.started and follow-up loop.progress. SHA-256 covers exact UTF-8 outgoing prompt bytes, including whitespace and injected corpus context. No prompt text is placed on the event. Full-text assets are private, immutable, owner-pinned and signed using existing media primitives. Hash-only creates no asset. Missing browser telemetry is null, not no. In hash-only mode, anyone holding a guess of a brief's text can confirm it against the plain SHA-256 hash. All entry points enforce WARP_BRIEF_MAX_BYTES = 1048576 (1 MiB) on the exact final UTF-8 prompt or follow-up message, including corpus prefix and separator, before any brief asset, attestation or Warp request. HTTP routes return 413; MCP tools name the byte limit in their error. A provider 4xx/5xx or network failure retains the recorded brief and adds a node-signed warp.brief.dispatch_failed attestation with only hash, assetId, upstreamStatus (null for network) and errorClass (http_4xx, http_5xx or network). Its contextId is assetId or the hash. The original provider error is rethrown even if failure auditing fails.

- GET /jin/api/brief-settings — Read the authenticated principal's Warp brief storage preference; security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 401, 403, 503
- PUT /jin/api/brief-settings — Change future brief retention with an atomic node-signed event; body: application/json (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 400, 401, 403, 503
- GET /api/cron/registry-app-expiry — Expire DCR clients that never completed consent after seven days; security: [{"bearerAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 401, 500, 503
- GET /jin/api/registered-apps — Read registered app lifecycle and provenance (node operator only); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]},{"bearerAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 401, 403, 503
- GET /jin/api/cloudflare-grants — List the controlled verified zone's operation grants; parameters: query:ownerDid (required), query:domain (required), query:zoneId (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]},{"bearerAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 403, 503
- POST /jin/api/cloudflare-grants — Delegate zone operations to another DID without repasting the token; body: application/json (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]},{"bearerAuth":[]}]; responses: 201, 400, 403, 503
- GET /jin/api/orgs/{ownerDid}/mail-senders — Read organization and per-app send-only sender settings; parameters: path:ownerDid (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 401, 403, 500
- PUT /jin/api/orgs/{ownerDid}/mail-senders — Save one fixed-purpose organization sender or per-app override; parameters: path:ownerDid (required); body: application/json (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 400, 401, 403, 500
- POST /jin/api/internal/session-events — Internal authenticated-socket handoff for signed plugin observations; body: application/json (required); security: [{"internalKeyAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 500
- POST /jin/api/runs/{loopId}/commands — Prepare or dispatch a principal-signed loop command; parameters: path:loopId (required); body: application/json (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 500, 503
- GET /jin/api/reach — List the signed-in principal's Reach Inbox; security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 401, 403
- POST /jin/api/reach/{reachId}/reply — Store and publish the principal's signed reply; parameters: path:reachId (required); body: application/json (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 400, 401, 403, 404, 409
- POST /jin/api/reach/{reachId}/block — Block the sender of a Reach card in one tap; parameters: path:reachId (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 401, 403, 404
- GET /jin/api/events — List personal or acting-as organization signed events (Record lane); parameters: query:kind, query:action, query:since, query:agent, query:grant, query:limit, query:offset; security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 400, 401, 403
- GET /jin/api/operator-approvals — List operator approval proposals across every connected source; parameters: query:history, query:view, query:source, query:count; security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 401

- POST /jin/api/vault-proposals — Raise a vault action as a canvas-native operator-approval card; body: application/json (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 201, 400, 401, 403
- POST /api/apps/provision — Propose apps.provision (#2375) — create/register/seal an extracted (third_party) app; body: application/json (required); security: [{"cookieAuth":[]}]; responses: 200, 201, 400, 401, 409, 500
